messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Cho <acho@rivermark.ai>, Sophie Li <sophie.li@rivermark.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: RiverMark discovery + technical follow-up

Hi Alex / Sophie —

Thanks for the time today. Short recap from our side and clear next steps so we can make the technical deep-dive efficient: we captured the pain, goals, and immediate asks below.

Key pain points you called out
- Inconsistent response times during monthly billing spikes (90–120s tail behind avg).
- Cost variability from your current self-hosted cluster + bursts causing budget overruns.
- Need for deterministic recovery for peak windows (no noisy neighbor impact).

Goals you shared
- 99th percentile request latency <= 120 ms at prompt lengths up to ~256 tokens (interactive assist flows).
- Sustained throughput target: 120 concurrent requests/sec for the assistant use-case; short bursts to 300 rps tolerated for ~10m windows.
- Data residency constraint: primary traffic in US-east, with a possibility of private deployment behind your VPC.
- Prefer open-model base (instruction-tuned Llama-family variant) but willing to evaluate Redwood-verified quantized builds.

Technical notes / assumptions (from today)
- Workload: short chat turns, KV caching applicable for context reuse; average output length ~80 tokens.
- Expected RPS distribution: 70% interactive, 30% batch inference (nightly queue).
- Security: SOC2/ISO audit evidence will be required for procurement; we'll supply standard artifacts.

Immediate next steps (action owners)
1) Kimberly: Share a concise requirements doc + an estimate sketch for Dedicated vs Private deployment + high-level cost delta — by EOD 10/26. (attachment: rivermark-sla-draft.pdf)
2) Marcus: Prepare a proposed deployment topology with GPU sizing and caching strategy; include a rough perf runbook and fallback policy — by 10/27.
3) Alex: Share a redacted sample of a high-latency request trace and a representative daily RPS histogram (or confirm we can use the sample logs you mentioned).
4) Priyom / Laura: We'll scope an initial POC plan (2-week guarded run) and outline success criteria for performance & regression.

Attachments included with this email: rivermark-sla-draft.pdf (stub), deployment-topology-sketch.png

If any of the bullets above don't match what you heard, please flag so we can correct before Marcus builds the topology. We'll schedule the technical deep-dive (Marcus + Priyom + your infra lead) after we get the sample logs.

Thanks again — excited to move forward.

— Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Kimberly — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from my side:

- Data residency: we need the model and inference to run inside our VPC / on-prem perimeter. Can Redwood Private be deployed into our AWS account (VPC peering / private control plane)?
- Latency target: 99th <= 120 ms is correct for interactive flows. For batch scoring we can accept higher latency, but throughput must not impact interactive SLA.
- Model: We currently use an instruction-tuned open model (variant of Llama-3 70B) with some adapter weights. We can provide a representative model artifact and a sanitized request sample.

I'll upload the redacted traces + RPS histogram into the Drive folder you shared by EOD tomorrow. Also attaching a short doc with our internal infra contacts.

One ask: please include a recommended fallback policy in your topology (e.g., lightweight small model for degraded mode) — we can't have frontend failures.

Alex

acho@rivermark.ai | +1 (617) 555-0244

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-10-26T08:11:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call: RiverMark discovery + technical follow-up

Alex / Team —

Thanks for the prompt notes. A few technical recommendations ahead of the scheduled deep-dive so we can target the POC correctly:

Summary recommendation (short)- Deploy Redwood Private into RiverMark's AWS VPC (private control plane) + a small Dedicated pool for canary traffic in our hosted region for cross-checking. Use model pinning so we can roll back to a quantized variant if needed.

Topology sketch (high-level)
- Front layer: autoscaled inference gateway (reduces cold-starts, TLS termination inside VPC).
- Serving pool: 2 node groups —
  * Primary: 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs (mixed precision / 8-bit quantized) for interactive requests and KV cache; target concurrency per GPU: 30–40 in steady state.
  * Fallback pool: 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs running a smaller distilled model (7–13B) for degraded mode.
- Cache: prefix/KV cache in Redis within VPC to reduce repeated context generation for chat flows.
- Autoscaling policy: scale up aggressively for 5–10 minute spikes (step scaling) and maintain a minimum reserve to handle billing-window bursts.

Performance estimate (rough)
- With quantized Llama-3 70B on H100-equivalent: expect 90–140 ms P99 depending on prompt length and KV hit rate. To reliably hit 120 ms P99, aim for 4 primary GPUs as sketched and 50–60% cache hit.
- If RiverMark cannot use H100-equivalent hardware, we will adjust GPU counts; we’ll provide a capacity table in the detailed doc.

Data and security
- Private control plane + customer VPC; logs and telemetry can be routed to your S3/KMS for retention. SOC2 artifacts: we will package standard evidence and a SOC2 readiness checklist for procurement.

Requested artifacts from RiverMark (so we can size POC)- redacted high-latency traces (sample)- RPS histogram (7-day)- a representative token-length distribution CSV

I'll compile the node-sizing table and a POC runbook (2-week guarded run) and circulate by COB 10/27. Forwarding the topology sketch to the Drive folder for your infra team.

—Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
